about: House recipes, batch 04 (slice B): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Sweet Potato Toddler Fingers
recipes.summary: Soft oat and cheese sweet potato fingers that little hands can hold, baked rather than fried.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a tray with baking paper. Boil the sweet potato for 12 minutes until very soft, drain and mash smooth.
Mix in the egg, oats, cheese, flour and cumin to a thick, sticky mixture.
With damp hands shape into 18 fingers about 6cm long and 1.5cm thick, set on the tray and brush with the oil.
Bake for 22 to 25 minutes, turning once, until golden and firm. Cool until just warm.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 3 fingers. Toddler snack.
Choking hazard: always sit toddlers down to eat and supervise them; serve soft and cooled, and break fingers into smaller pieces for babies under 12 months.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and bake until the fingers are firm all the way through; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep refrigerated for 2 days or freeze for 1 month.

recipes.title: Veggie Pancake Strips
recipes.summary: Soft zucchini and carrot pancakes cut into finger-sized strips.
steps: Whisk the flour, egg and milk into a smooth batter and stir in the zucchini and carrot.
Heat a little of the oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium heat. Pour in a sixth of the batter to make a 12cm pancake and cook for 2 minutes until bubbles appear and the underside is golden.
Flip and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until golden and set in the middle. Repeat to make 6 pancakes, then cut into strips.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 pancake in strips. Toddler snack.
Choking hazard: cut into thin strips for toddlers, seat them to eat and supervise them.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and cook until no wet batter remains; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep refrigerated for 2 days; reheat until warm.

recipes.title: Apple Oat Toddler Biscuits
recipes.summary: Soft biscuits sweetened only with apple, with no added sugar.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line two trays.
Mix the oats, flour, cinnamon and baking powder, then stir in the apple, egg and melted butter to a soft dough.
Roll into 20 balls, set 3cm apart on the trays and flatten to 1cm thick.
Bake for 16 to 18 minutes until golden and firm. Cool on the tray.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 biscuits. Toddler snack.
Choking hazard: seat toddlers to eat and supervise them; break biscuits up for younger children.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and bake until firm; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep airtight for 3 days.

recipes.title: Cheesy Broccoli Bites
recipes.summary: Little baked egg and cheese bites with hidden broccoli.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and grease a 12-hole mini muffin tin.
Mix the broccoli, cheese, eggs and breadcrumbs.
Spoon into the holes, pressing down, and bake for 18 to 20 minutes until golden on top and set in the middle. Cool in the tin for 5 minutes.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 bites. Toddler snack.
Choking hazard: chop broccoli very finely, seat toddlers to eat and supervise them; cut bites in half for young toddlers.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and bake until the centre is firm with no runny egg; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep refrigerated for 2 days.

recipes.title: Pea and Mint Fritters
recipes.summary: Soft green fritters with a mild cheese flavour, cooked in a little oil.
steps: Mash the peas roughly. Stir in the flour, egg, milk, cheese and mint to a thick batter.

Heat a little oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium heat. Drop in tablespoons of batter, flatten slightly and cook for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden and set in the middle. Make 18 fritters.
Drain on paper towel and cool until just warm.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 3 fritters. Toddler snack.
Choking hazard: mash peas well, seat toddlers to eat and supervise them; halve fritters for young toddlers.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and cook until the middle is set; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep refrigerated for 2 days.

recipes.title: Soft Pikelet Fingers
recipes.summary: Fluffy pikelets cut into fingers, lightly buttered for small hands.
steps: Whisk the flour, egg, milk and sugar into a smooth batter.

Melt a little butter in a non-stick frying pan over medium heat. Drop in tablespoons of batter and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until bubbles appear, then flip and cook for 1 minute until golden. Make 16 and cool.
Cut each pikelet into 2 fingers to serve.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 pikelets. Toddler snack.
Choking hazard: seat toddlers to eat and supervise them; skip thick spreads and cut up for younger children.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and cook until no wet batter remains; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep airtight for 1 day or freeze for 1 month.

recipes.title: Carrot Toddler Muffins
recipes.summary: Mini muffins sweetened with carrot and apple, with no added sugar.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and grease two 12-hole mini muffin tins.
Mix the flour and cinnamon, stir in the carrot and apple, then add the egg, milk and oil and fold until just combined.
Fill 24 holes two-thirds full and bake for 13 to 15 minutes until risen and a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tin for 5 minutes.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 mini muffins. Toddler snack.
Choking hazard: seat toddlers to eat and supervise them; break muffins up for younger children.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and bake until the centre is set; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep airtight for 2 days or freeze for 1 month.

recipes.title: Mini Frittata Toddler Squares
recipes.summary: Soft baked egg squares with zucchini, peas and cheese, cut for finger food.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Brush a 20cm square tin with the oil and line it with baking paper.
Whisk the eggs and milk, then stir in the zucchini, peas and cheese.
Pour into the tin and bake for 18 to 20 minutes until set in the centre and lightly golden. Cool for 10 minutes and cut into 24 squares.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 3 squares. Toddler snack.
Choking hazard: mash the peas lightly, seat toddlers to eat and supervise them; halve squares for young toddlers.
Food safety: bake until the egg is firm all the way through with no runny egg, cool quickly and keep refrigerated for up to 2 days; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep refrigerated for 2 days.

recipes.title: Zucchini Cheese Toddler Fingers
recipes.summary: Soft baked zucchini and cheese fingers with a golden crust.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a tray.
Mix the zucchini, egg, breadcrumbs and cheese to a firm mixture.
Shape into 18 fingers 6cm long, set on the tray and brush with the oil.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes, turning once, until golden and firm.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 3 fingers. Toddler snack.
Choking hazard: seat toddlers to eat and supervise them; break fingers into smaller pieces for younger children.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and bake until firm all the way through; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep refrigerated for 2 days.

recipes.title: Hiking Trail Mix Bars
recipes.summary: Chewy oat, nut and seed bars packed with slow energy for the track.
steps: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional). Line a 20cm square tin.
Mix the oats, nuts, sultanas and seeds. Warm the honey, peanut butter and coconut oil together and stir into the dry mix until well coated.
Press very firmly into the tin and bake for 22 to 25 minutes until golden at the edges and set.
Cool completely in the tin before cutting into 12 bars.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 bar. Contains peanuts and tree nuts. Plus 1 hour cooling.
Storage: wrap individually for hiking; keeps 2 weeks.

recipes.title: Honey Oat Energy Balls
recipes.summary: No-bake oat, peanut butter and honey balls for the daypack.
steps: Mix everything in a bowl until the mixture holds together when squeezed.
Roll into 16 balls the size of a walnut.
Chill in the fridge until firm to the touch.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 balls. Contains peanuts. Plus 30 minutes chilling.
Storage: keep refrigerated for 1 week; packed in a cool bag they hold for a day's hike.

recipes.title: Puffed Rice Sports Bars
recipes.summary: Crunchy honey and peanut butter bars that give a quick carbohydrate hit before or during exercise.
steps: Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Warm the honey and peanut butter in a pan over low heat for 2 minutes until runny and smooth.
Stir through the puffed rice, oats and seeds until evenly coated, then press very firmly into the tin.
Chill until firm, then cut into 12 bars.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 bar. Contains peanuts. Plus 1 hour chilling.
Storage: keep airtight for 1 week.

recipes.title: Savoury Rice and Cheese Recovery Slice
recipes.summary: A baked rice, egg and vegetable slice with protein and carbohydrate for after training.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Grease and line a 20cm square tin with the oil.
Beat the eggs, then mix in the rice, cheese, zucchini, carrot, corn and spring onions.
Press into the tin and bake for 28 to 30 minutes until golden and firm in the middle. Cool for 10 minutes and cut into 8 slices.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 slice.

Food safety: cool cooked rice within 1 hour and keep it refrigerated; use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs, bake until the middle is firm and reheat leftovers until piping hot; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep refrigerated for 2 days.

recipes.title: Homemade Grissini
recipes.summary: Long thin crisp breadsticks made with olive oil and a little sesame.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast and salt, add the oil and warm water and knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Cover and let it rise until doubled.
Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line two trays.
Roll the dough to a 20cm by 30cm rectangle and cut into 20 strips. Stretch each to 30cm, set on the trays and sprinkle with sesame.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp when snapped. Cool on a rack.
notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 2 grissini. Contains sesame. Plus about 1 hour rising.
Storage: keep airtight for 1 week.

recipes.title: Sesame Simit Sticks
recipes.summary: Crisp-chewy sesame-coated bread sticks inspired by Turkish simit.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast and salt, add the oil, honey and warm water and knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Cover and let it rise until doubled.
Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line two trays.
Divide into 16 pieces, roll each into a 20cm stick and roll in the sesame seeds.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until golden and crisp on the outside. Cool on a rack.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 sticks. Contains sesame. Plus about 1 hour rising.
Storage: keep airtight for 3 days.

recipes.title: Olive Oil Cracker Crisps
recipes.summary: Thin crisp crackers with oregano and flaky salt.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line two trays.
Mix the flour, salt and oregano, then add the oil and water to a firm dough and knead for 2 minutes.
Roll as thin as possible, cut into 32 rectangles and prick with a fork.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes until golden at the edges and crisp when cooled. Cool on a rack.
notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 4 crackers. Plus 15 minutes resting the dough.
Storage: keep airtight for 1 week.

recipes.title: Wholemeal Za'atar Crackers
recipes.summary: Crisp wholemeal crackers with thyme, sesame and sumac.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line two trays.
Mix the flours, salt, thyme, sesame and sumac, then add the oil and water to a firm dough.
Roll as thin as possible, cut into 32 squares and prick with a fork.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes until crisp and golden at the edges. Cool on a rack.
notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 4 crackers. Contains sesame. Plus 15 minutes resting the dough.
Storage: keep airtight for 1 week.

recipes.title: Soft Bavarian Pretzel Sticks
recipes.summary: Chewy pretzel sticks with a deep brown skin, dipped in a bicarbonate bath before baking.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, add the warm water and butter and knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Cover and let it rise until doubled.
Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line two trays. Divide the dough into 20 pieces and roll each into a 15cm stick.
Bring the water and bicarbonate of soda to the boil. Lower in a few sticks at a time for 20 seconds each until they puff slightly, lift out with a slotted spoon and drain.
Set on the trays, sprinkle with flaky salt and bake for 12 to 15 minutes until deep brown and firm.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 sticks. Plus about 1 hour rising.
Use care with the boiling bicarbonate bath: it can splash and should not be touched while hot.
Storage: best the day they are baked.

recipes.title: Garlic Bread Chips
recipes.summary: Thin crisp bread squares baked with olive oil, garlic and oregano.

items: 8 slices day-old white bread, cut into 3cm squares

steps: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional) and line two trays.
Toss the bread squares with the oil, garlic powder, oregano and salt.
Spread in a single layer and bake for 12 to 15 minutes, turning once, until dry, golden and crisp. Cool on the trays.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: about 20 chips.
Storage: keep airtight for 1 week.

recipes.title: Paprika Pitta Chips
recipes.summary: Crisp pitta triangles with smoked paprika, ideal for dips.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line two trays.
Split each pitta into 2 rounds, brush with the oil and sprinkle with paprika and salt. Cut each round into 6 triangles.
Bake for 8 to 12 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp. Cool completely.
notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 1 pitta (12 pieces).
Storage: keep airtight for 1 week.

recipes.title: Parmesan Crisps
recipes.summary: Crisp lacy cheese rounds with black pepper, high in protein and low in carbohydrate.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a tray with baking paper.
Mix the cheese, pepper and rosemary and spoon 24 small mounds onto the tray, 3cm apart, flattening each slightly.
Bake for 5 to 6 minutes until lacy and golden brown at the edges. Cool on the tray to crisp.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Gluten-free. Per serving: 4 crisps.
Storage: keep airtight for 2 days.

recipes.title: Fennel Taralli
recipes.summary: Crunchy Puglian ring snacks with fennel seeds, boiled and then baked.
steps: Mix the flour, fennel and salt, add the oil and water and knead for 5 minutes into a smooth dough. Rest, then roll into 24 ropes of 10cm and join the ends to make rings.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line two trays. Boil the rings in batches in a pan of water for 1 to 2 minutes until they float, then drain on a tea towel.
Bake for 22 to 25 minutes until golden and crisp. Cool on a rack.
notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 3 taralli. Plus 30 minutes resting the dough.
Storage: keep airtight for 2 weeks.

recipes.title: Rosemary Polenta Crackers
recipes.summary: Crumbly buttery crackers with a corn crunch and rosemary.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line two trays.
Rub the butter into the polenta, flour, salt and rosemary, then add the water to a firm dough.
Roll to 3mm thick, cut 24 rectangles and prick with a fork.
Bake for 13 to 15 minutes until golden at the edges and firm. Cool on a rack.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 3 crackers.
Storage: keep airtight for 1 week.

recipes.title: Chilli Cheese Crackers
recipes.summary: Crisp buttery cheese crackers with a hint of chilli and smoked paprika.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line two trays.
Rub the butter into the flour, then mix in the cheese, chilli and paprika and add the water to a firm dough.
Roll to 3mm thick and cut 30 rounds with a 4cm cutter.
Bake for 12 to 14 minutes until golden and crisp at the edges. Cool on a rack.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 3 crackers. Plus 30 minutes chilling the dough.
Storage: keep airtight for 5 days.
